channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Israeli Report on Soldiers Using Palestinians as Human Shields Ignites National Backlash
item.description: Public outcry over the TV investigation highlights nation’s struggle to come to terms with allegations over how it fought the war in Gaza.

item.title: Inside China’s $4 Billion Secondhand Luxury Boom
item.description: Watch WSJ’s Hannah Miao explore one of China’s biggest resale megastores to understand what’s behind the country’s shifting consumer habits.

item.title: BAE Systems Secures $6 Billion in Combat-Vehicle Contracts For Several European Nations
item.description: The arms maker secured contracts to supply hundreds of combat vehicles as European nations seek to buttress their armed forces amid high geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Canada Posts Current-Account Surplus of C$4.48 Billion
item.description: Canada posted a third-quarter current-account surplus, marking the first time in about four years the country has recorded two consecutive quarterly surpluses, though it was smaller than expected.

item.title: France Slips Into Recession as Exports Sag
item.description: The French economy tipped into a recession in the third quarter as summer heat waves slowed Airbus’s factories.

item.title: Oil Prices Mixed Ahead of OPEC+ Meeting as Middle East Supply Risks Persist
item.description: Oil prices were mixed on Friday as traders weighed renewed threats to Middle Eastern supplies ahead of a meeting of OPEC and its allies during the weekend.

item.title: Inflation Slides in France, Spain on Declining Fuel Prices
item.description: Inflation fell more than expected in November, while the eurozone economy grew less rapidly than previously estimated in the three months through September.

item.title: Chinese Shares Lifted as Beijing Signals More Market Support
item.description: Authorities reiterated support for capital markets and vowed stabilization policies, amid increased volatility in global markets.

item.title: New Zealand Election Ends in Deadlock, Turns Outsider Into Kingmaker
item.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon needs support of newcomer Qiulae Wong’s Opportunity Party to form majority government.

item.title: No Homes to Rent, No Way to Evict: Inside Spain’s Housing Crisis
item.description: The dysfunctional market for homes has become a politically explosive issue at the ballot box—and a warning for everyone else.

item.title: The AI Boom Looks Alive and Well in Asia
item.description: Stocks are having a wild ride thanks to the Nvidia affair, but AI-linked exports and investment are still driving growth—for now.

item.title: Iranian Drone Attack Kills Two Italians in Kuwait
item.description: The attack hit as technicians from Rheinmetall Italia worked on an air-defense system.

item.title: Europe Has Picked a New Central Bank Chief. He’s in for a Bumpy Ride.
item.description: Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to take over from Christine Lagarde at the ECB next year.

item.title: Nvidia Tells Partners to Pause Shipments to Southeast Asia
item.description: Washington recently closed a remote-access loophole that helped Chinese companies tap in to computing power in the region.

item.title: As Another Wartime Winter Sets In, Kyiv Residents Weigh Finally Leaving
item.description: Russia is pummeling Ukraine’s power lines and generating plants, making everyday life a survival mission.

item.title: A Game-Changing Move Just Gave America the Edge Over China in AI
item.description: Washington closed a loophole that let Chinese companies access Nvidia chips and added overseas cops to curb smuggling.

item.title: BOE Warns Scale and Breadth Of AI Financing Poses Threat to Financial Stability
item.description: The AI investment boom is supporting global economic growth, but the scale and breadth of financing that it requires is making the global financial system more vulnerable to setbacks, the central bank said.

item.title: Bank of England Proposes Cut to U.K. Bank Capital Requirements
item.description: The measures would release more capital to be used on dividends, buybacks or lending, and the central bank said it could free up more capacity to lend to U.K. households and businesses.

item.title: UniCredit Seeks Commerzbank Chair Role for CEO Orcel After Takeover Clears Final Hurdle
item.description: The Italian bank said it received approval from Poland’s financial regulator, satisfying all regulatory conditions for its takeover of the German lender.

item.title: New Tariffs on China Risk Undermining Trade Truce With U.S.
item.description: China warns it could retaliate if the administration goes ahead with the duties.
